title: Elodie and the Border
premise: Orsen Blackwood, a crash investigator haunted by the deaths of his wife and daughter in row twelve, is confronted by Elodie Vasseur, a stranger who claims he once saved her life — a favor he never performed. Elodie's 'debt' pulls him into a conspiracy: the crash that killed his family was no accident, and the evidence proving it is the one secret a powerful airline syndicate will kill to bury. As Orsen and Elodie's wary alliance deepens into love, he must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the last person he has left, trading the evidence for her life. In the end, he leaks the truth publicly at devastating personal cost, finds a fragile justice outside the law, and begins, finally, to sleep.
about_author: Ulyana Thackeray is a former air-safety analyst who left the field to write fiction about the people behind the accident reports. She lives near the coast, where she claims the fog helps her plot.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Eighteen months after the crash, Orsen works nights investigating minor incidents, unable to sleep through the night. On the anniversary, a woman named Elodie appears at his office claiming he saved her life years ago. He remembers no such thing. Emotional beat: grief interrupted by a crack of mystery.

chapters.title: A Debt Never Owed
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Elodie insists on repaying the phantom favor with information: the crash file was altered, and someone inside the investigation board signed off on it. Orsen dismisses her, but checks the archive and finds his own signature on a document he never signed. Emotional beat: disbelief curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Forged Hand
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie reveals she's a former claims adjuster who discovered the forgery while processing payouts — and that her discovery got her colleague killed. She needs Orsen's access and expertise. He refuses; she leaves him a burner phone anyway. Emotional beat: reluctant complicity, two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Tailwind
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen quietly re-examines the flight data and finds a maintenance override logged minutes before impact — a pattern consistent with sabotage. That night his apartment is searched. Emotional beat: the investigation stops being grief-work and becomes survival.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A syndicate fixer named Corben contacts Elodie, offering money for the file and veiled threats about her sister. She stalls, then calls Orsen on the burner. They meet in a rail yard and compare what they know. Emotional beat: trust forged under pressure, first flicker of tenderness.

chapters.title: The Quiet Passenger
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen identifies the override's author: a board director tied to the airline's insurer, and discovers his family's row-twelve seats were a targeted consequence — his wife had witnessed something. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; the case becomes personal vengeance he must keep leashed.

chapters.title: Dead Reckoning
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie's sister is taken as leverage. Elodie trades the only copy of the file for her sister's release, hiding from Orsen that the evidence is gone — and that she kept a single page back. Emotional beat: love against duty; betrayal committed for the right reasons.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen learns the trade happened and feels the betrayal, but decodes the withheld page — a ledger linking Corben to the director. Corben corners them; a violent escape through the docks costs Orsen a gunshot wound. Emotional beat: fury, forgiveness, and the decision to finish it together.

chapters.title: The Long Descent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. Orsen and Elodie broadcast the ledger and flight data during the board's public inquiry, forcing a confession on live feed while Corben hunts them through the terminal. Corben is arrested; the director's empire cracks; Orsen, bleeding, chooses testimony over escape. Emotional beat: justice seized outside the law, at full cost.

chapters.title: First Light
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue. Months later: hearings concluded, indictments filed, Elodie's sister safe. Orsen visits the crash memorial, leaves row twelve behind, and sleeps through the night for the first time — waking to Elodie making coffee. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into love; the border crossed.
